subject.title: Add Herdr state bridge for OpenClaw TUI

question: Should Herdr pane-state reporting be a plugin-gated bundled plugin, explicit core-owned TUI behavior, or kept outside core until a generic TUI lifecycle plugin seam exists?
rationale: The PR adds a new env-triggered runtime integration and a default-on bundled plugin shell, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent ownership boundary or user-facing policy.

options.title: Gate Through Plugin Policy
options.body: Accept Herdr as a bundled plugin only if sidecar startup honors resolved plugin enable, deny, allowlist, and per-entry disablement decisions.

options.title: Make It Core-Owned
options.body: Treat ambient `HERDR_PANE_ID` as explicit core TUI behavior, remove the misleading no-op plugin wrapper, and document the env-triggered surface as core-owned.

options.title: Defer Outside Core
options.body: Pause or close this PR until a generic TUI lifecycle/plugin seam exists or Herdr can ship as an external ClawHub package without core-specific wiring.

recommendation.title: Gate Through Plugin Policy
recommendation.body: Accept Herdr as a bundled plugin only if sidecar startup honors resolved plugin enable, deny, allowlist, and per-entry disablement decisions.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is primarily about plugin/core product boundary, and history shows repeated ownership of plugin policy docs and TUI/runtime seams.
